project_callout.title: Bring your research challenge. Build it with the community.
project_callout.body: Turn a technical roadblock, early-stage idea, or ongoing open-science project into a collaborative Brainhack project. Projects of every size are welcome, and first-time project leaders are encouraged to apply.

gb10_highlight.title: 20 Dell Pro Max with GB10 systems available
gb10_highlight.intro: Thanks to the generous support of Dell Technologies and NVIDIA, attendees will have access to 20 compact AI workstations during the hackathon.

services.name: Get Involved
services.short: Find exciting projects that you would like to contribute to.
services.title: Open hacking
services.desc: sessions for attendees to work together on projects of their own design. Attendees are encouraged but not required to bring their own projects into the hackathon to work collaboratively with others. Project inspirations could stem from other projects proposed by attendees, ongoing work you're involved in, or new research areas that you've been waiting to have an opportunity to jump on!

services.name: Share
services.short: Show your research to other neuroscience researchers.
services.title: Unconference
services.desc: is the perfect opportunity to showcase bits of your latest research, spark interest in a new initiative/project, or make an announcement of interest to the Brainhack community.

services.name: Gain Skills
services.short: Learn how to apply the latest computational tools to your data.
services.title: TrainTrack
services.desc: to help you get up to speed with various programming languages, current practices in open-source, and reproducible neuroscience analysis.

services.name: Network
services.short: Meet researchers from a variety of backgrounds.
services.title: Network
services.desc: with the community throughout the hackathon and an evening social event!

tutorials.title: Managing Research Software Projects
tutorials.description: This workshop introduces the ideas and tools you need to manage a team of up to a dozen people working together to build research software. Each session ends with something you can take home and use the following week.
tutorials.speaker: Dr. Greg Wilson
tutorials.bio: Dr. Greg Wilson is a programmer, author, and educator based in Toronto. He co-founded and was the first Executive Director of Software Carpentry, and has authored or edited over a dozen books. Greg is a member of the Python Software Foundation and a recipient of ACM SIGSOFT's Influential Educator of the Year award.

tutorials.title: Introduction to Git and GitHub
tutorials.description: This workshop teaches the basics of version control using the local software Git and the collaborative online platform GitHub. It is meant for beginners and will provide you with the necessary theoretical knowledge and practical skills to get started with these two important software tools.
tutorials.speaker: Dr. Julia-Katharina Pfarr
tutorials.bio: Julia is a PostDoc at McGill working on methods for clinical questionnaire harmonization. She has given the introductory workshop to Git and GitHub at least a dozen times.
